summary.title: Four Cool URLs
summary.one_liner: Four real-world examples (Goodhertz presets, Reddit .json, Combine.fm, Traintimes.org.uk) show how well-designed URLs can act as presets, APIs, portable links and human-editable queries.
takeaways: A URL can be the thing itself, such as a plugin preset or a search query, not just a pointer to a page.
Appending .json to many Reddit URLs gives a JSON version without needing an API key or OAuth setup.
Predictable, human-editable URLs let users and scripts build links without extra documentation or a middleman service.
Good URLs are descriptive and robust, so links keep working even if a third-party service disappears.
summary.summary: The author walks through four URLs that do more than identify a page: a Goodhertz Vulf Compressor preset URL that both configures the plugin and renders as a readable page, Reddit's .json suffix that exposes an API without registration, Combine.fm links that map a music track to multiple streaming services, and Traintimes.org.uk URLs that can be edited by hand to change station, time and day. Each example is used to draw general principles, such as URLs being robust, predictable, human- or machine-oriented, and descriptive. The post closes by noting these principles do not fit every case, such as news article links or unguessable document links.
